replacement.title: Turn around the traffic
replacement.objective: Turn into space that avoids a teammate and the defender while keeping the puck protected.
replacement.briefing: Navy attacks the right net (+x). YOU carry in the neutral zone; F2 is directly up ice from you and D1 is closer to the middle. Space beside them may offer a turn, depending on how both players move.
cues: D1 is offset inside that route.
A side space is visible beside the traffic.

questions.prompt: Who is directly up ice from YOU?

options.text: F2
D1
No one

questions.explanation: F2 is directly ahead of YOU in the scene.

questions.prompt: Which two relationships belong in the turn?

options.text: F2's path ahead
D1's inside position
The promise that the outside space stays open

questions.explanation: The teammate and defender both affect the turn. Re-check the outside space as either moves.

questions.prompt: Arrange this controlled-turn plan.

options.text: See F2 and D1
Move toward the available side space
Protect the puck and re-check the lane

questions.explanation: The turn changes the angle, then the puck and lane must be checked again.

questions.prompt: Move YOU beside the traffic into a possible turning space.
questions.explanation: This point leaves F2 ahead and D1 inside, giving YOU a changed angle without assuming the space is empty later.

questions.prompt: F2 moves toward the same outside space. What should YOU reconsider?

options.text: A different turn or support lane that avoids crowding F2
Keep turning into F2 because the space was named
Pass blindly through D1

questions.explanation: F2 moving toward that space may narrow your turning route. Recheck the gap and pressure before choosing a different turn, a pass or a protected touch.

questions.prompt: Why must a turn account for F2 as well as D1?
questions.explanation: F2 can occupy or open the turning lane. A good turn keeps both players in the scan so the puck stays protected while the next option changes.

replacement.objective: Choose a receiving angle that leaves room to protect the first touch.
replacement.briefing: Navy attacks the right net (+x). F1 has the puck in the neutral zone. YOU are farther up ice on the same side of the middle. D1 is up ice from YOU and closer to the middle; F2 is wider on the other side. Offer a receiving target only if F1 can reach it.
cues: D1 is farther up ice and closer to the middle than YOU.
F2 is across the middle and may offer a continuation after reception.

replacement.title: Bank the puck off the wall
replacement.objective: Use a wall option to change the route around a defender, then read the rebound.
replacement.briefing: Navy attacks the right net (+x). F1 owns the puck between the middle and the side boards. D1 is near the direct route to YOU, who are farther up ice and wider. F2 is closer to the middle; D2 is farther toward the right net. A bank off the side boards is one possible route to assess.
cues: D1 is near the direct passing route.
YOU are farther up ice and wider than D1.
F2 is closer to the middle; D2 may affect that option.

D2

questions.explanation: D1 is near the line between F1 and YOU. The freeze does not prove stick reach or an interception.

options.text: Where the rebound would leave YOU and D1
Whether the inside option to F2 stays clear of D2
That the wall sends the puck to the same spot every time

questions.explanation: The wall changes the route but not the need to read the rebound, pressure, and inside support.

options.text: See D1 and the wall space
Choose a reachable bank point
Read the rebound before the next touch

questions.prompt: Move YOU toward the side boards, farther up ice than D1, to offer a possible bank-pass target.
questions.explanation: The example moves YOU closer to the side boards and farther up ice than D1. F1 still needs to judge a reachable bank point and rebound; no bounce or completed pass is guaranteed.

options.text: Whether the wall route or F2 lane is now more reachable
Bank the puck without looking because D1 moved
Pass through D1 to the original spot

questions.explanation: D1 turning toward the boards is a cue to reassess, not proof that a route closed or opened. Compare the bank option with F2 and D2 before choosing.

questions.prompt: How is a wall option different from simply passing through D1?
questions.explanation: It changes the puck route around the defender and creates a new rebound to read. The option remains conditional on the rebound and support.

Under D1’s control

options.text: Can YOU reach the actual puck before D1?
Which teammate can support after control?
Can YOU follow the original plan without locating the loose puck?

questions.prompt: Arrange this missed-pass response.

options.text: Locate the actual puck and D1
Approach with control
Re-scan F1 and F2 after recovery

questions.prompt: Move YOU closer to the loose puck, then recheck D1.
questions.explanation: This example reduces the distance to the loose puck. Recheck D1 while approaching; the marker does not prove a safe route, visibility or control.

The puck returned to F1

questions.prompt: What could you say to F1 after the pass misses?
